subject: Preflight: environment gate spot-check + comms plan
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lyle <sam@clearline.io>, ops@clearline.io
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Preflight: environment gate spot-check + comms plan

Hi Sam / Clearline ops,

Quick preflight before we schedule the formal network acceptance call next week. I pulled together a short spot-check list to confirm the high-risk items we usually see during private deployment handoffs. If you can answer the three bold items below by EOD tomorrow, we can lock the intake window and reduce the go/no-go risk.

Snapshot checklist (ask each item with short answer):
- Public egress: Can you confirm the list of outbound IP ranges that will be used for the inference control-plane and telemetry? (we need 3x /24s or single NAT EIP set)
- KMS access: Do you have a reachable KMS endpoint with cross-account policy in place? If yes, share the principal ARN and test key id.
- Firewall + port matrix: We only need to allow ports 443 and 5222 for control-plane; management bastion needs 22 from our maintenance IPs. Please attach the current firewall rules export.
- DNS delegation: Do you plan to provide a private zone or will Redwood manage split-horizon records?
- Monitoring/Agents: Can the environment run our lightweight telemetry agent (containerized) with egress to telemetry.redwood.ai:443?

Outstanding blockers we often see (for visibility):
- Unexpected NAT translation for KV-cache replication causing higher token latency
- Missing CIDR documentation for service endpoints (blocks canary smoke tests)
- KMS policy missing enablement for encryption/decryption by our service principal

Attachments: I attached the minimal VPC diagram we received and an example firewall csv for format. Please reply with the exported firewall file and a short answer to the three bold items.

Next steps (internal): Ben / Kim — if Sam gives the green light on egress/KMS/fw we run the smoke traffic on Wed 10/07 10:00–12:00 PT. If any answer is partial, we'll extend to Thu for remediation verification.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0198
Attachments: clearline_vpc_diagram.pdf (diagram), fw_rules_snapshot.csv (CSV export)
From: Sam Lyle <sam@clearline.io>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@clearline.io, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: environment gate spot-check + comms plan

Thanks, Aisha — quick answers below and attaching the firewall export.

On Tue, Oct 6, 2026 at 9:12 AM Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Snapshot checklist (ask each item with short answer):
> - Public egress: Can you confirm the list of outbound IP ranges that will be used for the inference control-plane and telemetry? (we need 3x /24s or single NAT EIP set)

We will provide two static EIPs for now (54.201.22.18, 54.201.22.19). We're evaluating a /24 allocation with infra this quarter but it's not in place yet.

> - KMS access: Do you have a reachable KMS endpoint with cross-account policy in place? If yes, share the principal ARN and test key id.

Yes — KMS is provisioned in the infra account. Principal: arn:aws:iam::998877665544:role/clearline-redwood-kms-access. Test key id: 1234abcd-5678-ef90-gh12-ijklmnopqrst (will rotate per policy).

> - Firewall + port matrix: We only need to allow ports 443 and 5222 for control-plane; management bastion needs 22 from our maintenance IPs. Please attach the current firewall rules export.

Attached (fw_rules_snapshot.csv). We currently also have health-check probes from our upstream LB on 8080 — we'll remove those for the redwood-managed paths before the smoke test.

> - DNS delegation: Do you plan to provide a private zone or will Redwood manage split-horizon records?

We will provide a private hosted zone and give Redwood the ability to create A/AAAA entries under redwood.internal.clearline.local.

> - Monitoring/Agents: Can the environment run our lightweight telemetry agent (containerized) with egress to telemetry.redwood.ai:443?

Yes. Egress allowed to telemetry.redwood.ai. Ops will whitelist our outbound EIPs noted above.

Summary: main gap is the /24 egress expectation — we can proceed with the two EIPs but would like to understand the contingency if we exceed burst allocations. Happy to join the smoke window Wed 10/07.

Sam
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Clearline Health
Attachments: fw_rules_snapshot.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Lyle <sam@clearline.io>, ops@clearline.io
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: environment gate spot-check + comms plan

Thanks Sam — this is helpful. Two quick internal notes and actions for clarity:

On Tue, 06 Oct 2026 14:08:00 -0700 Sam Lyle <sam@clearline.io> wrote:
> Summary: main gap is the /24 egress expectation — we can proceed with the two EIPs but would like to understand the contingency if we exceed burst allocations.

1) Contingency: Aisha / Ops — we will add a short fallback in the rollout plan: if token-level egress exceeds expected thresholds during the first 30m of smoke traffic, Redwood will automatically route new requests to our hosted fallback model and throttle back batch sizes for the private deployment until infra scales NAT. This will be a temporary mitigation; we must capture metrics and escalate if sustained.
2) Validation tasks for the smoke window (Wed 10/07 10:00–12:00 PT):
   - Redwood: run 10k sample tokens through the canary model, measure p95 latency and token egress.
   - Clearline ops: confirm KMS decrypt for a test key and confirm agent telemetry ingestion.
   - Joint: validate DNS records and ensure the management bastion only accepts connections from our maintenance IP list.

Kim — can you draft the short fallback paragraph and the telemetry runbook entry? I'll assemble a one-page intake note to attach to the acceptance ticket and share with Clearline.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Aisha: I'll queue the intake note and create the smoke-test Jira (CLEARLINE-ONB-12) and attach the firewall snapshot and VPC diagram submitted by Sam.
